source.title: Source
source.description: Where to read the certificate, as a URL: `https`, `tcp`, `tcp4`, `tcp6`, `udp`, `udp4` or `udp6` for a TLS server, `smtp` for an SMTP server with STARTTLS, `file` for a local PEM file.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: Certificate retrieval timeout, in seconds. Covers the connection, the SMTP exchange and the TLS handshake.

tls_skip_verify.title: Skip TLS verification
tls_skip_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate and hostname verification, so certificates that are self-signed, expired or issued for another name are still read.

tls_ca.title: TLS CA
tls_ca.description: Path to a CA bundle used to verify the server certificate. Leave empty to use the system trust store.

tls_cert.title: TLS client certificate
tls_cert.description: Path to a client certificate file for mutual TLS. Requires a client key.

tls_key.title: TLS client key
tls_key.description: Path to the client key file for mutual TLS. Requires a client certificate.

check_full_chain.title: Check full chain
check_full_chain.description: Report the expiration time of every certificate the source presents, including intermediates and the root, not only the server certificate.

check_revocation_status.title: Check revocation status
check_revocation_status.description: Check whether the server certificate has been revoked, using the CRL and OCSP endpoints listed in it.

autodetection_retry.title: Detection retry
autodetection_retry.description: How often to retry the initial connection when the job fails to start, in seconds. Zero disables retries.

source.ui:help:
Network sources need a port.

- Website: `https://example.com:443`
- Other TLS service, such as LDAPS or SMTPS: `tcp://ldap.example.com:636`
- SMTP with STARTTLS: `smtp://smtp.example.com:587`
- Local file: `file:///etc/ssl/certs/example.com.pem`

timeout.ui:help: Accepts decimals for precise control (e.g., type 1.5 for 1.5 seconds).

vnode.ui:help: Charts of this job appear under the Virtual Node instead of this host. Define the Virtual Node in `vnodes.conf` first, then enter its name here.
